A1.justification: Both PDFs describe NaviMaster and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices. Content can be matched reliably across section renumbering and figure relocation.

before.justification: v2 reports original GUI, spatial-affordance, and ObjectNav evaluations in Tables 1–3, along with ablations and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v3 retains these original evaluations and adds ObjectNav baseline results, reward ablations, threshold experiments, and training-data statistics.

M1.justification: The visual-target collection algorithm, action spaces, history-conditioned GRPO, and three reward components remain unchanged. Indicator notation replaces equivalent piecewise rewards. Zero depth maps for 2D inputs and history truncation are newly documented implementation details, not established changes to the method.

E1.justification: Training sources and evaluated GUI, spatial-affordance, ObjectNav, and visual-relation tasks are retained. The new ablations reuse AC-High/Low, Where2Place, and RefSpatial. VIS-Bench is cited for motivation but is not newly evaluated.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds RoboPoint and SpaceLLaVA to the ObjectNav comparison, previously containing Qwen2.5VL-7B and NaviMaster variants. These methods already appeared in the spatial-affordance comparison, but their ObjectNav participation is new. Other comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Tables 8–11 introduce controlled reward omissions, absolute versus relative thresholds, distance thresholds of 100–400 pixels, and depth thresholds of 0.1–10 m or no depth gate. Existing splits, metrics, and training budgets remain unchanged. H.4 describes normalized relative-threshold training prospectively despite reporting its results.

E4.justification: Beyond v2's sparse-versus-dense reward and reward-weight analyses, v3 separately tests format/type reward removal, absolute versus relative thresholds, distance sensitivity, and depth removal/sensitivity. Appendices G.6 and H substantially expand evidence about component necessity and reward robustness. Existing data-mixing, model-size, data-source, and case-study analyses are retained.

E5.justification: New Appendix G.1 states that all reported results are averaged over multiple trials and discusses inference variability. v2 lacked this repeated-run disclosure. No run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests are supplied; the statement does not establish an increase in runs.

E6.justification: v3 substantially expands diagnostic results through Tables 8–11. For example, Table 11 reports Where2Place scores of 52.97 with a 1 m depth threshold versus 36.84 with 0.1 m. Table 3 adds RoboPoint at 13.01 SR/2.80 SPL and SpaceLLaVA at 14.98/2.62; Figure 6 adds action frequencies. Retained benchmark and ablation values are unchanged, including NaviMaster's 33.20 SR/12.60 SPL.

T1.justification: The substantive MDP formulation, projection equations, GRPO advantage, and action-space definitions are retained. Reward expressions use equivalent indicator notation. The cognitive framing and circle-area calculation explain existing choices without introducing a new formal result, proof, or substantive mathematical construction.

C1.justification: The introduction newly characterizes unification as an egocentric-to-allocentric cognitive transformation and asserts isomorphism at the perception and decision-making level. The three principal contributions and the abstract/conclusion claims about unified training and generalization otherwise remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 substantially expands interpretation through cognitive framing, sampling-bias and stability arguments, and Appendix H's explanations of absolute thresholds, reward hacking, resolution, and depth. Depth is newly qualified as a robustness safeguard rather than a principal performance source. G.6 also attributes gains to instruction adherence, although its claim of declines across all benchmarks contradicts Table 8. The original limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 documents oldest-step truncation below 7000 tokens, distribution-preserving GUI-Odyssey sampling, zero depth maps for 2D inputs, vLLM inference temperature 0, minimum GUI resolution 1280×720, and embodied resizing to 1980×1080. Its abstract explicitly advertises code, data, and checkpoints at a revised project address; v2 only advertised a homepage. Existing hardware and training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Thinking in Space/VIS-Bench to motivate cognitive unification and the PagedAttention/vLLM reference for inference implementation. Existing positioning against GUI agents, embodied agents, Embodied Web Agents, and OmniActor is largely retained.

P1.justification: Editing is localized to the introduction, reward notation explanations, and expanded appendices. The Overview subsection heading is removed, training settings gain subsections, and the threshold appendix shifts Case Study from H to I. Most existing prose and the overall narrative sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds the GUI-Odyssey distribution chart and Tables 8–11, expands and relabels Table 3, and relocates Figure 2 from page 4 to page 3. Existing plots and qualitative examples are retained with limited formatting and numbering changes; there is no broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The added ObjectNav comparisons, reward controls, and implementation disclosures improve the paper's diagnostic support and reproducibility. These gains are limited by incomplete statistical reporting and overstated interpretation: G.6 claims universal declines, while Table 8 shows improvements on RefSpatial without format reward and AC-Low without type reward. The additional evidence remains useful despite these weaknesses.
